_README: Project-level permission policy for STEM Quest. Committed on purpose: a fresh
clone should arrive with guardrails already on.
Denies outrank allows across every settings layer, so the deny list below wins
over the pre-approvals in the (gitignored) settings.local.json. That file is
left alone deliberately — nothing here requires editing it.
The active deny list is the prod-destructive set only. Merging a PR deploys the
backend on Render and the frontend on Cloudflare Pages, so `gh pr merge` is a
production action and belongs to the human; /finish-phase says the same thing.
DELIBERATE DEVIATION: mcp__neon__run_sql and mcp__neon__run_sql_transaction are
NOT denied. They are one tool for both reads and DDL, and the established
post-deploy verification workflow uses them to read production. Denying them
would remove that read access, so they sit in `ask` instead. Honest note: any
MCP tool that is not explicitly allowed already prompts, so listing them under
`ask` changes nothing functionally today. Its value is that it survives someone
later adding a broad mcp__neon__* allow — the explicit `ask` would still hold.
Bash deny rules are a SAFETY NET, NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY. They are evaluated
per-subcommand across &&, ||, ;, | and newlines, but a wrapper such as
sh -c '...' is a documented gap in that matching. .claude/hooks/guard-bash.sh
is what closes that gap; the deny list alone does not.
This file is tracked in a public repo. No secrets, no private hostnames.
INERT. `_proposed` is an unknown top-level key, so the settings parser ignores
it — nothing in here is enforced. It is staged policy, written down while the
reasoning was fresh, for a later phase to activate.
Activation is a one-line move: the arrays below mirror the real shape, so a
rule is turned on by cutting it from `_proposed.<list>` into
`permissions.<list>`. Move rules one at a time and re-test — a deny that fires
on a command the phase loop actually needs is worse than no deny at all.
`_rationale` maps each rule string to the specific thing it stops. If a rule
cannot be given a concrete threat there, it does not belong in the list.

_rationale.Bash(git push --force:*): Rewrites published history on a branch CI has already run against; on main it is blocked by branch protection, but a force-push to a feature branch still destroys review context mid-PR.
_rationale.Bash(git push -f:*): Same as --force. Listed separately because deny matching is literal on the command prefix.
_rationale.Bash(git reset --hard:*): Discards uncommitted work with no recovery path. Phase work is often hours of uncommitted rules/spec edits.
_rationale.Bash(rm -rf:*): One bad path expansion removes the working tree. Nothing in the phase loop needs recursive force-delete.
_rationale.Bash(docker compose down -v:*): The -v flag wipes the postgres volume — the entire local database, including whatever was being reproduced.
_rationale.Bash(gh workflow run:*): The repo ships db-backup.yml and demo-reset.yml. Both act on PRODUCTION. A manual dispatch from a session is a production write with no confirmation.
_rationale.Bash(env): Dumps every environment variable, secrets included, into a transcript that gets screen-shared during demos and interviews.
_rationale.Read(./.env): Real local credentials. Note: .env.example is tracked and useful, which is why this lists exact files rather than a Read(./.env.*) glob that would also swallow the example.
_rationale.Read(./backend/.env): Django SECRET_KEY, database URL, Resend and Sentry keys.
_rationale.Read(./frontend/.env): Build-time VITE_* values, including the Sentry DSN.
_rationale.Read(~/.ssh/**): Private keys. Nothing in this project needs them read.
_rationale.Read(~/.aws/**): Cloud credentials outside this project's blast radius.
_rationale.mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*: Personal mail. Connected for other work, irrelevant here, and the highest-consequence surface in the tool list.
_rationale.mcp__claude_ai_Canva__*: Unrelated connector; denying keeps the tool surface matched to the project.
_rationale.Bash(git push:*): Pushing a feature branch is normal, but it is also the point where work becomes public in a public repo. Worth one prompt.
_rationale.Bash(pip install:*): A dependency bump ships third-party migrations that must be checked against Neon, and re-runs both CI audits. Never a silent action.
_rationale.Bash(npm install:*): Same: changes the lockfile, re-runs npm audit --omit=dev in CI, and can pull a new transitive advisory.
_rationale.Bash(python manage.py migrate:*): Migrations are applied by render.yaml's preDeployCommand, never by hand. A local hand-apply desynchronises the two.
_rationale.Write(./backend/*/migrations/**): A migration file is the highest-risk artifact this project produces — it runs while the OLD code is still serving.
_rationale.Edit(./backend/*/migrations/**): Editing an applied migration silently diverges the recorded schema from the real one.
_rationale.Edit(./render.yaml): Defines the production service, its env vars and the preDeployCommand. A wrong edit here is a production outage.
_rationale.Edit(./.github/workflows/**): The CI jobs are the only gate on main. Weakening one is invisible in a green PR.
_rationale.Edit(./.gitignore): This is a public repo with five private docs and settings.local.json held back by exactly this file.

_keys.permissions.defaultMode: Candidate. Would set the baseline prompting behaviour for the session instead of relying on per-rule lists. Not set here because the phase loop mixes long unattended stretches with interactive ones and the right default differs between them.
_keys.permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode: Candidate value "disable", which would stop --dangerously-skip-permissions from turning every rule above off. UNVERIFIED: research returned contradictory answers on whether this key takes effect outside managed/enterprise settings. Do NOT activate it on the strength of this file — confirm against the current docs first, and if it only works in managed settings, say so here and drop it.
_keys.enableAllProjectMcpServers: Candidate value false, so a newly added .mcp.json server is not auto-enabled for every session. Currently governed by enabledMcpjsonServers in settings.local.json.
